description: Build-time architecture resolution in docker/base-image/Dockerfile (Abilityai/lilu#263). The image pinned two x86-only artifacts by name and so could not be built on the arm64 DGX it is built for, and the two halves fail in OPPOSITE directions — which is why a single static check is not enough. `opencode-linux-x64@<ver>` is a DIRECT npm target, so arm64 rejects it LOUDLY (EBADPLATFORM, 4.8s into step 11/40); being a direct target is exactly the property #257 wanted against npm's silent-optional path, so the explicit platform-package naming is asserted to SURVIVE and only its NAME to be resolved. `go1.23.4.linux-amd64.tar.gz` fails SILENTLY: on arm64 that URL exists, downloads and untars with no error, spending 641s installing a toolchain that cannot execute — so the in-layer `go version` assertion against the RESOLVED `linux/${goarch}` is pinned, in the SAME RUN as the download, because a separate layer would still cache and publish the bad install. The mapping is not re-typed: the `case "$(uname -m)"` blocks are EXTRACTED from the shipped Dockerfile and EXECUTED under a `uname` shell-function stub (a function shadows the external command and is inherited by command substitution, so no executable stub file is needed on a noexec /tmp), asserting x86_64 and aarch64 resolve to the artifacts verified to exist upstream and that an unmapped machine EXITS NON-ZERO naming the architecture rather than defaulting — a default is how #263 happened. npm and Go spell x86 differently (x64 vs amd64) and arm64 identically, so the two mappings are asserted independently rather than shared. Also fences the reverse regression (swapping one hardcoded arch for the other) and pins `uname -m` over `TARGETARCH`, which is EMPTY under the classic builder — the same silently-wrong-artifact class — and whose in-stage ARG would sit above the Go layer and bust the cached upper layers that make a DGX retry cheap. Never builds an image; no Docker daemon required (gap:engineer-no-docker-daemon).
